study_identification.title: Regional, circuit and network heterogeneity of brain abnormalities in psychiatric disorders

study_characteristics.study_objective: To characterize the heterogeneity of gray matter volume (GMV) differences in six psychiatric disorders and to test the hypothesis that anatomically heterogeneous regional GMV deviations are functionally coupled with common sites.

dataset_name.answer: Multi-site aggregated dataset (ABIDE I; ABIDE II; ASRB; FEMS; and 10+ other studies)

hc_age.answer: min 18; max 64; mean and sd not reported

quality_checking_detail.answer: Visual inspection for artifacts (53 exclusions); CAT12 IQR > 2.8 (153 exclusions); processing pipeline failure (63 exclusions).

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) with site and sex effects modelled with random slopes, intercepts and noise.

predictor_effects.answer: Site and Sex are random effects; Age is a fixed effect.

diseases_studied.answer: ADHD; ASD; BP; MDD; OCD; SCZ

clinical_groups_age.answer: ADHD: median 34 (10) [18-61]; ASD: range of medians 22-43, range of ranges 18-64; BP: median 32 (11) [18-64] and 21 (2) [18-26]; MDD: median 26 (11) [18-52] and 30 (9) [19-55]; OCD: median 29 (9) [19-53] and 35 (9) [18-58]; SCZ: range of medians 31-39, range of ranges 19-64

clinical_groups_sex.answer: ADHD: 41.18% male, ASD: 100% male, BP: 47.37% male, MDD: 34.16% male, OCD: 50.30% male, SCZ: 62.14% male

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: No association analysis with clinical variables was performed.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Person-specific deviations from population expectations for regional GMV were highly heterogeneous, affecting the same area in <7% of people with the same diagnosis. However, these deviations were embedded within common functional circuits and networks in up to 56% of cases.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: The salience-ventral attention system was implicated transdiagnostically, with other systems selectively involved in depression, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder. Phenotypic differences between cases assigned the same diagnosis may thus arise from the heterogeneous localization of specific regional deviations, whereas phenotypic similarities may be attributable to the dysfunction of common functional circuits and networks.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Subtle brain changes, use of multi-site data with different protocols, lack of correlation with clinical variables, use of DSM/ICD criteria, and focus on GMV.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The paper introduces a new framework to integrate normative models of GMV with elements of lesion network mapping.
